title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Handyman
audience: Handyman owners who want repeat visits and referrals from landlords, property managers and households they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Make a review or referral request after the client confirms the result, and make it easy to decline
Write a next-visit offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it
Write referral reward terms, including the payment condition, before any referral is made

instruction.heading: Ask after the client confirms the result
instruction.body: Ask for a review or a referral after the client has checked the finished tasks and paid, not while you are still on site. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you want, such as a review or the name of one person who might need a handyman, and make it easy to decline. Record the date and the answer. Timing matters: in one Baylor Keller Center experiment, 1.32 per cent of customers left a review with no reminder, against 2.16 per cent with a late reminder. That is one experiment, not a rule. A marketing association piece (AMA, January 2023) says that some services need more time before customers can judge them, so match the timing to the work.

instruction.heading: Keep review requests within the platform rules
instruction.body: A review link or QR code is allowed, and Google provides one. Do not write reviews for clients, invent them, or ask only the happy clients, which is called review gating. Google bans discounts or goods in return for reviews, including reviews that change or remove a negative one. The ACCC says any incentive must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Check each platform's terms before offering any incentive.

instruction.heading: Offer the next visit before the client leaves
instruction.body: Handyman work often leaves a list behind: a door to re-hang next month, a gate to adjust after winter, a second floor of shelves. At sign-off, propose the next visit with a date, the scope, and the price approach. Confirm the client agrees before you change their schedule. If the offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase.

instruction.heading: Check in at an interval that suits the work
instruction.body: A check-in about ninety days after a repair is a choice to test, not a benchmark. Ask whether the work still holds, whether anything has changed and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short and factual. A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder, so check it against the Spam Act before you send it.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward, such as a credit on the next visit, and write the payment condition, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. Give the referrer a copy. A 2023 study in the Journal of Marketing Research found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across seven studies, so say what the reward is in the invitation. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent. Check any cash-based reward, and its tax and contract effect, with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points are not settled here.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-visit offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the work, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A handyman completes a door adjustment and two cupboard hinge repairs for a landlord who owns two rental properties in the same street. She says she will recommend him to a friend who also rents out a house nearby. He wants to offer a credit on the next visit if the friend books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should he do before the friend books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes the terms before any referral happens: the credit, the condition that the friend completes a paid job, and the date the credit is applied. He asks his client to pass on the friend's details, and he contacts the friend only if the friend agrees. He does not promise a reward he has not written down, and he sets the size of the credit from his own margin rather than from any published figure. He checks whether the work is inside his licence and insurance. For example, a referred job above the Queensland $3,300 building licence threshold, or NSW minor maintenance above $5,000 including GST, needs a licence he holds. A referral does not extend his licence. If he is unsure of the tax or contract effect of the credit, he confirms it with an adviser before he starts.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-visit offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal dates for check-ins
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has checked the finished tasks.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo or review without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or accepting a referred job outside your licence.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and honour it at once. Check the licence and insurance before accepting any referred job.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. Whether the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business is not settled in the research; check the OAIC's small business guidance.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder. Every commercial message needs a working unsubscribe, honoured within five working days.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only work your licence and insurance cover in the state where it is done. Queensland and NSW thresholds differ, and Victorian licence rules for some handyman tasks are not settled in the research. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-visit offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer
Next-visit offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next visit in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or referral?
options: Before the first task starts, so the client feels committed
Only after the client has sent a complaint
After the client has confirmed the finished tasks are right

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to post a review with their name and a photo of the finished shelves. What do you need?
options: Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional
The client's consent for the name and photo you plan to publish

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does this lesson say to propose the next visit?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only: 1.32 per cent versus 2.16 per cent with a late reminder.

AMA, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Timing should match how long customers need to judge the service.
Google Business Profile Help, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Review links and QR codes; no discounts or goods for reviews.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on review content.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; describes filtering review invitations by sentiment as review gating.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Stating the reward in the invitation increased referrals. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older than 2022. Used for the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Factual service reminders can still be commercial messages.
ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown. Consent, identification and unsubscribe; honour within five working days.

Queensland Building and Construction Commission, 'Licence required for building work', https://www.qbcc.qld.gov.au/node/7081, last reviewed 16 April 2026. Licence above $3,300 including materials, labour and GST.

NSW Government, 'Minor maintenance and cleaning work', https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/minor-maintenance-and-cleaning-work, last updated 23 June 2026. Licence above $5,000 in labour and materials including GST.
